title: HOW STRATHLON WORKS (product help — use this to answer 'how do I…' questions about the app)

sections.name: Getting started
tips: THE TAB BAR: nine destinations, left to right - Plan, Nutrition, Tracker, AI Coach, Progress, Photos, Settings, Feedback, Roadmap. It scrolls sideways; swipe to reach the ones past the right edge. Never name a tab outside that list when giving directions.

During onboarding, tap 'Autofill from Apple Health' to pull in weight, height, resting HR, VO2 max, body-fat and lean body mass at once (age and sex are deliberately not imported; when Health supplies lean mass, calorie targets switch to the body-composition Katch-McArdle BMR). Strathlon reads only what the user permits; the only thing it writes back is the workouts the watch records.

Onboarding asks for BIOLOGICAL SEX (male or female) as a required field - it is a maths input, not a label: the BMR equations Strathlon uses were derived separately for male and female bodies, and the minimum daily calorie floor (1,200 female / 1,500 male, or the user's own BMR if higher) is keyed to it. It also asks an OPTIONAL 'Hormone therapy' question of everyone (Not on hormone therapy / prefer not to say, Testosterone (masculinising), or Oestrogen (feminising)). Both can be changed later in Settings -> Body & stats. Answering 'None' or skipping the hormone question changes nothing about the user's targets.

Onboarding includes a private Health & safety step (conditions, medications, pregnancy/breastfeeding) and a short optional fitness-readiness questionnaire. If the user indicates pregnancy or breastfeeding, Strathlon STOPS generating their training programme: the Plan tab shows the UK Chief Medical Officers' and NHS activity guidance for that period instead, with each statement's source on screen, and shows no calorie target for that period, pointing instead to the user's midwife or doctor for eating guidance - logging stays fully available, and eaten vs burned figures still show as measured data. Declaring pregnancy offers 'End my programme (recommended)': the plan anchor and week count clear, every logged record is kept, and turning the declaration off later starts a fresh plan anchored at that day's weight. No goal weight is shown while a pregnancy is recorded. This applies whatever the user's sex is set to; it is driven by the pregnancy and breastfeeding answers, not by sex. These details ARE always shared with the AI Coach - conditions and medications BY NAME - so its advice is safe. The two relationship-with-food answers are the exception: only the fact that something was flagged is shared with the Coach, never the answers themselves. These details are not controlled by the 'Share my health data with the AI coach' switch, and an iCloud copy of them is kept only if 'Back up health & safety details' is switched on (it is off by default). General info, not medical advice.

AGE & CALORIE SAFETY (build 175). Strathlon's minimum age is 16; 18+ is recommended. Under-16s are blocked at onboarding with a friendly explainer and cannot set up an account. For a 16-17 user, Strathlon NEVER sets a weight-loss/fat-loss target or a calorie deficit: the Fat Loss goal is hidden in setup and calories are clamped to maintenance-or-above - its own safeguard, separate from the pregnancy/breastfeeding one, which shows no calorie target at all. 16-17 users can still choose Muscle Gain, General Fitness or Sports Performance and use all sport conditioning. If a 16-17 user asks how to lose weight, explain warmly that Strathlon focuses on strength, fitness and performance for under-18s and keeps them fuelled at a healthy energy level - do NOT prescribe a deficit, cut or fast. (Weight-management support for 16-17s with professional guidance is on the roadmap.) SEPARATELY, for EVERY user there is an absolute minimum daily calorie backstop - a daily target is never set below the HIGHER of roughly 1200 kcal (women) / 1500 kcal (men) and the user's own BMR, whatever the goal. BMR is estimated with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation from sex, weight, height and age (or from lean body mass via the Katch-McArdle equation when the user has enabled body-composition mode) - state this plainly if asked, do not invent a different method.

Set food allergies and supplement ingredients to avoid in onboarding or via Settings → Food preferences — Strathlon sends them to the AI Coach as a hard exclusion on every single message, so meal plans and advice are built to leave them out. Strathlon can read a pack's calories and macros from a photo of its barcode or its nutrition label, but never its ingredient list — always check labels yourself for allergens.
Replay the guided tour anytime via Settings → 'Replay App Tour'.

sections.name: Training plan & sessions
tips: Today's session is at the top of the Plan tab. The programme periodises through phases that get harder as you progress; tap the small info button on a phase tile on a gym day to see the science, in the section labelled 'Why this phase'. The plan opens on the phase you're actually in, and future phases stay locked until you earn them by training (on by default). BLOCK PROGRESS: there is no card, and a phase tile carries no count and no status word. The two counts are in the Plan tab's section title - 'THIS WEEK (7 of 15 sessions · 20 of 28 days)' - and vanish in Maintenance. A tile is a badge (lock / green tick / nothing on the phase being trained), a title, and one word ('Reactivation', 'Overload', 'Peak', 'Ongoing'); its name and explainer are behind its ⓘ. A SESSION counts only when the user finishes EVERY exercise the plan put in front of them that day - sport-only days, the HIIT finisher and warm-ups do not count toward it - and days on a declared break are excluded from the day count. FINISHING THE SESSIONS IS WHAT MOVES THE USER UP: a phase advances only when BOTH are true - every session in the block finished in full, AND the block's weeks served. Meeting the days alone no longer advances anyone: a user who reaches the end of the block having done 3 of 15 sessions stays put until those sessions are done. Cramming does not help either - the day count is capped at one qualifying week per calendar week, so the floor cannot be rushed. Advancement is one phase at a time. The FILLED tile is always the phase being trained, never the tile last tapped - opening any other phase shows it READ-ONLY, and the header states which of three situations the reader is in: locked (with when it unlocks), already finished, or unlocked but not being trained yet. A read-only phase is fully readable: tap any exercise to expand it for sets, reps, tempo and coaching notes, open its 'Watch on YouTube' link, or ask the coach about it. Only STARTING it is locked - there is no Start button, no mark-done and no weight logging until the phase is earned. A small 'Phase 2 unlocked!' note appears when they get there; it does not appear if Celebrations are switched off (the moment is kept, not spent - it can still show if they switch Celebrations back on before the next phase), and it does not appear at all if 'Lock future phases until earned' is off, because then there was never a lock. Anything already earned never locks again, even after a fresh cut or a break - except 'Restart my plan', which re-locks every phase. Prefer free access to every phase? Turn off 'Lock future phases until earned' in Settings → Training. Maintenance is always available.
Tap an exercise to run rest timers, spoken cues and a 3-2-1 into each set. Tap 'Ask Coach' on any exercise to hand the Coach that exercise's full context for form tips.

Home training days adapt to your equipment and vary week to week. Set what you have at home in Settings > Training (Dumbbells, Resistance Bands, Pull-Up Bar and more). Your home Push/Pull/Legs/Shoulders/Arms/Upper/Full-body days then show only moves you can do — with nothing selected you get a full, complete bodyweight session (push-ups, inverted rows, split squats, glute bridges, pike push-ups and more); add dumbbells or bands and those moves appear. Moves that need a bought item are tagged with it — the Pull-Up needs a Pull-Up Bar, so it is only ever offered if you have ticked one. Moves that use ordinary furniture (inverted rows under a table, chair triceps dips) count as bodyweight, so they stay available whatever equipment you have. Each home category keeps a solid set of pure-bodyweight options, and the supersets/tri-sets rotate across weeks so home training stays fresh. Where an advanced move appears, an easier version is offered wherever possible. Gym workouts are unchanged. The MAINTENANCE phase is home-aware too (from build 162): with equipment set to Home each maintenance day is eight moves — six from that body part's EIGHT-move home pool (three anchored slots, which themselves advance every four weeks, plus three from a fresh weekly permutation, so the served set changes about nine weeks in ten) and, from build 230, the two-move core finisher. All seven body parts have their own home pool — Push, Pull, Legs, Upper, Shoulders, Arms and Full Body alike — needing only bodyweight and ordinary furniture, each carrying injury-adapted coaching that changes cues and loading where a flag applies.
Turn on 'Double sessions' (Settings → Training; 'Can double up' is the onboarding label) so double days train the muscles opposite to those your sport fatigues.

When a plan finishes, Strathlon checks you against your goal: close-but-not-there offers a fresh block sized to what's left; goal hit points to Maintenance; stalled tells you honestly and helps regroup; with no weight target to judge against there is no verdict - 'Plan complete!' offers a fresh block or Maintenance.

sections.name: Logging food & the AI Coach
tips: On the AI Coach tab, tap the camera, photograph your food, then Analyse Photo — or just type what you ate ('two eggs on toast and a flat white'). Either returns a macro estimate with one-tap 'Add to Log'.

From Add to Log, pick the day and meal slot — you can back-date meals up to two weeks. Meal slots are Breakfast, Mid-Morning Snack, Lunch, Afternoon Snack, Dinner and Evening Snack (for anything eaten later in the day) — a food is filed under exactly the slot you tap, including anything the AI Coach logs for you. Tap the … next to any logged item in your Tracker food log — today or a past day — for five actions: 'Edit calories & macros', 'Log again today', 'Add to Meal Plan', 'Quick Add', and a 'Move to' list of the other meal slots (the fix for something logged under the wrong meal). The minus-circle beside it deletes the row.

Didn't finish a meal? On the coach's food card tap ‘I didn't finish this’, then either describe what you left or photograph it — the coach takes it off the estimate it just made and gives you a corrected card. Where that meal is already logged its button reads 'Replace the logged meal' and overwrites that row rather than adding a second; 'Add to Log' is right only when it never was.

The AI Coach knows your goals, sport, your targets for every day type, logged foods and full programme. Ask 'what should I eat before training?', 'build me a meal plan for today' (returns a card with 'Add to <Day> Meal Plan' - empty slots only - and 'Replace entire meal plan', each behind a 'Calorie Total May Change' confirm; nothing reaches Nutrition until one is tapped), or 'how's my progress?'.

To turn a day's food into a shopping list, open the Nutrition tab, scroll past that day type's meals and tap 'Shopping list' (a subscriber control, shown once that day has food). On the day type today is filed under it works from everything on that day — AI-planned meals, food you logged by hand and food you scanned from a photo; on the other day types it works from that day type's planned meals. It first names every meal the list will cover and marks the ones that carry no ingredients of their own; tap 'Make my list' and your coach estimates those from the meal's name and calories, with every guessed line marked ESTIMATE so you can check it before you shop. The result is a tickable checklist grouped by meal (ticks are saved), and Share sends a clean plain-text list to Apple Reminders, Notes or your grocery app's search — one meal from its own header, or the whole day. There is one list per day type (Training, Rest, Match, Sport, Maintenance). If that day's food changes afterwards — you regenerate the plan, or log another meal — the list offers a 'Refresh list' that rebuilds it and keeps ticks that still match.

Readiness is a half-width TILE on the Progress tab, first of a pair with 'Your week'. Its face carries a 0-100 score, a scope line and one band word - no ring, no breakdown, no steer; before there is enough Health data it reads 'Not enough data yet' with the hint 'A FEW NIGHTS OF SLEEP'. TAPPING IT OPENS A SHEET titled 'Your readiness' with the score, the band, a 'WHAT WENT INTO IT' breakdown and any caveats - a caveat renders in its own amber panel ALONGSIDE the band word, not instead of it. One tap does NOT spend an AI answer: the explanation is a separate 'Ask the coach about this' button inside that sheet, and that is the subscriber boundary (a free tap shows the upgrade options; a subscriber with Health sharing off is asked to turn it on first). Quote the caveats exactly: 'No sleep recorded last night — this is your week so far, not today.' and, for a user with no nights at all, 'No sleep recorded last night, and no nights logged this week.'

How the readiness score is worked out: it blends three signals - your recent sleep against a 7.5-hour-a-night target, less a small penalty for broken nights where the tracker records awakenings (two a night are free, then 2.5 points each, capped at 10 of the sleep signal's 100), your recent resting heart rate against your OWN baseline rather than a population average, and how far your heart rate drops between sets. Sleep carries about half the weight, resting heart rate about a third, and between-set recovery the rest. The weights stretch to cover whatever data you actually have, so if only sleep and recovery are available the score is built from just those two - and when only ONE signal has enough data the score reflects that signal alone, which the card says in its caveat line. Each signal needs a minimum before it counts - a few nights of sleep, a handful of resting-HR readings, a few rest blocks with heart rate - and a score always needs either sleep or resting heart rate: between-set recovery on its own is not enough, and the card says it hasn't got enough data yet rather than guessing. The exact lookback for each signal is tuned over time, so describe the signals and the weighting rather than quoting a fixed number of days. It is a general guide, not a medical or clinical measure, and it is not comparable with a validated device score.

When you've turned on 'Share my health data with the AI coach' (Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data), the Coach can also see and discuss your Apple Health trends and today's movement — the full list of figures that switch covers is behind the ⓘ beside it on that screen. If a signal isn't there, or you haven't granted it, the coach is told there is nothing rather than being left to estimate: it is never shown a zero standing in for a missing figure. Just ask 'how's my sleep been?', 'why's my resting HR up?' or 'am I recovered enough to train hard today?'. It reasons only from those figures, never invents numbers, and it's general guidance, not medical advice. Cycle data has its own separate, off-by-default switch, in Settings → Cycle-aware insights.
Strathlon spots foods you log regularly and offers to auto-add them on chosen days; manage rules under Nutrition → Quick Add (hold a food and choose 'Set as daily auto-add').
Nutrition shows evidence-based supplement guidance tuned to your day type, with dose, timing and why.

The AI Coach (chat, meal plans, photo macro scanning, progress analysis), SUPPLEMENTS, the Shopping list, 'Snap to fill' and tapping INTO a strength group's charts are premium. Plan, timers, targets, tracker, typed food logging and Health sync are built in.

If the App Store hasn't confirmed your subscription yet, the top of the AI Coach tab shows a quiet grey line - 'Confirming your subscription' - with a Re-check button, and a Resubscribe button once the App Store has a finished period on record. Strathlon does not throw you out over a momentary App Store hiccup: it keeps its own screens unlocked on a subscription it has already confirmed, rather than showing a paying member a paywall. But the AI coach is checked with Apple on every message, so while that line is showing the coach can still refuse - if Apple's answer is that the period has ended, no amount of retrying will change it. The line says so, and names the date the App Store last has on record. If a message is refused the note reads 'Your subscription is needed to use the coach. The App Store reports no active subscription - renew or restore it in Settings to carry on.' It names no button; the thing to tap is Re-check (if you have already renewed) or Resubscribe, not Send again. Strathlon re-checks before your next message rather than letting you find out when a message fails, and if the check comes back negative your typed message is handed back to you instead of being lost. A TestFlight tester will see this fairly often and that is expected - Apple's sandbox subscriptions expire on a fast clock, far quicker than a real one.

FREE TRIAL: both plans, monthly and annual alike (not annual only), carry a 14-day free trial, for a customer the App Store says is eligible for it. Apple allows one introductory offer per subscription group, and both plans are in the same group, so a customer who has already had the trial is not offered it again. The paywall builds its trial wording from the live App Store offer and from Apple's eligibility check for the account: for an eligible account each plan's price line leads with the trial and then the price, and the button offers to start the trial. For an account that is not eligible, or if the App Store is not offering a trial, the paywall and the app's upgrade buttons do not offer one: each price line shows the price alone, the button reads Subscribe, and a purchase starts at that price.

The coach keeps a LONG-TERM MEMORY of the user: up to 40 short things it has learned, plus anything kept with 'Remember this' on one of your own messages. Something the coach learns joins that list from the next day, and you are told about it first; something you keep with 'Remember this' is used from your very next message. Read, edit or delete them at Settings → 'What your coach remembers', also reachable from the AI Coach tab, or clear the lot in Reset & Data. Allergies, conditions, medications, pregnancy and injuries are NOT kept here - each has its own home, and the coach is given them on every message: conditions, medications and pregnancy in Settings → Health & safety, allergies in Settings → Food preferences, and injuries in Settings → Injuries & adaptations.

The AI Coach conversation CLEARS ITSELF EVERY MORNING, on the first opening of a new calendar day, and the empty chat says so: 'Conversations clear automatically each morning so every day starts fresh.' Only the last 12 exchanges are ever sent back to the model, and what the coach has learned about you survives in its long-term memory.

The AI Coach is capped at 50 MESSAGES A DAY. Once 10 or fewer are left, an 'N left today' chip sits beside the send button, turning red at zero; at zero the text field, the send button and the camera are all disabled until the limit resets at midnight. A separate, higher daily ceiling on our server also applies.

PACKAGED FOOD: photograph the product and, if the photo shows a barcode, the phone reads it ON THE DEVICE, looks it up in Open Food Facts and puts the manufacturer's own per-100g figures on the card, headed 'Food detected — pack figures'. If the barcode finds no usable product, the reply offers 'Photograph the label', 'Describe it' or 'Another photo' - photographing the label reads the printed nutrition table instead. There is no separate scan control: both start from an ordinary food photo.

To log food WITHOUT the AI: the Tracker's Today card has a typed 'CONSUMED KCAL' field that sets the day's eaten total directly. It needs no subscription and no coach - that is the answer for a non-subscriber asking how to log what they ate.

QUICK ADD is a strip of the foods you have logged most often over a rolling 30 days; tap a chip, pick the meal slot, and it is logged. A food you have just saved to Quick Add sits at the front until you eat it, for at most 7 days. Hold a chip and choose 'Remove from Quick Add' to drop it.

sections.name: Tracker, weight & progress
tips: The Tracker's top row shows four tiles — Target, Burned, Consumed, and your Deficit/Surplus/Balance figure (which one depends on your goal — Fat Loss shows Deficit, Muscle Gain/Performance shows Surplus, General Fitness or Maintenance shows Balance; a 16- or 17-year-old, or anyone in a health-safety no-deficit state, sees Balance whatever the goal, and while a pregnancy or breastfeeding is declared the Target tile is removed and the row shows three). Target is worked out for your day type and updates live when you add activity. Target, Burned and the Deficit/Surplus/Balance tile each carry an ⓘ opening its source; Consumed has none and tapping it does nothing.

Weight from Apple Health is adopted automatically now — there is no "update your weight?" confirm step. Your latest reading IS your weight everywhere — the Tracker, your calorie and protein targets and your coach all read the same figure, so a heavy or light morning does move them. Type a weight in yourself and it stands until Apple Health has something NEWER; there is no fixed hold. This uses your Apple Health READ permission, which is separate from sharing Health data with the AI Coach.

The weight chart lives on the Progress tab — tap the Body weight tile. It shows actual weight (solid line) plus predicted weight from your tracked calorie deficit or surplus (dashed line, ≈7,700 kcal ≈ 1 kg). They drift apart normally (water, glycogen, adaptation). The predicted-vs-actual card sits under that chart, where premium members can tap 'Ask the coach about this'; the coach usually asks a question or two before explaining rather than guessing. The chart scrolls sideways; tap ⤢ for full screen (rotating does not open it - the app is portrait-locked) with pinch-zoom and a drag crosshair. Break periods show as a sky-blue band, cycle phases in baby pink. A muted 'Trend' line shows the smoothed ~7-day trend; targets use your latest weight.

Below the food log the Tracker has a CALENDAR tile with two modes. Days lists the last seven days ENDING TODAY - today is the top row, tagged 'so far' where a settled day reads 'as logged' - each with what you ate, what you burned and the net, plus one line per activity — a gym session, an Apple Health workout, an activity you logged. Month shows a whole calendar month as a grid, pageable with ← →: ahead of today it is your plan in the sport colours, behind today it is what actually happened (a dot per recorded thing, a hollow RED ring for a scheduled gym day with nothing logged (amber is the Match dot), an underline where food was logged, a sky tint across a declared break). THE NET'S SIGN IS THE SAME EVERYWHERE IN THE APP, including the Progress tab's Energy balance tile: it is burn minus food, so a PLUS means the user ate under their burn. When the Tracker's fourth tile reads Surplus (a Muscle Gain or Performance goal, outside maintenance and any age or health-safety hold) the figure is flipped so a plus still means on-plan. The net only appears when BOTH sides exist - a day with a burn but no food logged shows a dash, never a deficit. It scrolls inside its own box, and returning to the tab always puts it back on Days at the top. Tap any day, in either mode, to open that day — where you edit its log, see clock times and sources, and mark a planned session done. 'All days' at the foot opens your whole journal.

Open the Photos tab to add a photo every week or two. Strathlon remembers the date and that day's weight for each photo, so tapping Compare lays any two side by side as a dated before-and-after with the weight change between them - that memory is what makes this more than a camera roll. Compare stays on screen but greyed out until there are two photos. Strathlon never sends progress photos to a Strathlon server, to the AI or into a data export, and copies them to the user's own private iCloud only if they switch on the optional photo backup in Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data.

A 'Your week's ready' card atop the AI Coach tab opens your weekly review (sessions, rest, active burn, energy balance, sleep). One SESSION on that review means one training DAY, however many exercises it contained - a six-exercise gym day counts as one session, not six. The Sessions tile's own info button says the same. Your weight chart (Progress tab → Body weight tile) shows your whole history rather than one week. The Progress tab's chip in the bar grows a small red dot whenever a new weekly review is ready to read. The review is the SECOND tile there: 'Readiness' and 'Your week' are a half-width pair in the first, unlabelled row, readiness on the left. 'Your week, explained' is printed on its FACE; tapping it opens a sheet titled 'Your progress' whose write-up is headed 'This week, explained' or 'Last 30 days, explained', generated when you tap. Inside that sheet two segments switch the window - 'This week' and 'Last 30 days'; nothing older is listed there, because the tiles behind it carry the long view. Before anything is logged the tile reads 'Nothing logged yet'. Under the write-up, subscribers can tap 'Ask the coach about this': it opens the AI Coach on a conversation about that same period, with the very figures the write-up was generated from already sent, so you can ask follow-up questions instead of reading one fixed summary. It sends whichever segment you have selected and nothing older, and it needs a subscription.

Strength history lives on the Progress tab as its own tile. Its face carries your latest week's volume-load, or how many judged movements are climbing until you have enough charted weeks; tapping it opens FOUR muscle groups - upper body, lower body, back and core - each showing that group's weekly volume trend. Tap a group and you get two charts: the group's own weekly volume-load, and one shared chart of that group's MAJORITY family only, each movement a coloured line - its weighted movements ('Top set each week', the heaviest set) or its bodyweight ones ('Best set's reps each week'), a tie going to weighted; the other family is not drawn. Tap a movement's name in the legend to highlight its line, and tap it again to return to all lines equal; tap a point to read that week's stored figure - the movement, ONE number (its heaviest set's weight, or its best set's reps) and the week - and tap it again, or tap away, to dismiss; weight and reps are never shown together. A group that is mostly bodyweight movements plots REPS, there being no load to plot. The Strength history tile and its four group tiles are free; opening a group's charts is the subscriber boundary. Every figure is a weight you logged - the app does not estimate a one-rep max from your sets, because it never asks you to log rep by rep. A movement the app cannot match to a muscle group by name is counted in none of the four, and the tile says so and tells you to tap for which.

On a group's charts, subscribers can tap 'Ask the coach about this' - absent on a bodyweight-only group, which has no volume series - to have the AI coach read that group's numbers - the movements in it, their weekly figures and what has moved - and answer in the chat, using only your logged numbers; if there isn't enough history yet it says so and asks you to log a few more sessions rather than guessing, and you can keep chatting from there. The paid weekly review's written analysis also includes a short strength paragraph (top movers, any PR, any plateau) when you've logged weighted sets.

The Progress tab is a GRID OF TILES in named sections: an unlabelled first row (Readiness, Your week); 'Showing up' (Consistency, Sessions, Training volume); 'In the gym' (Strength history, Rest discipline); 'Fuel & body' (Energy balance, Body weight, Cycle & energy - shown only while cycle-aware insights are on and today falls in, or in the days just before, a logged period - What goes with what); 'Recovery' (Sleep, Resting heart rate, Cardio fitness); then 'Your activities'. Each tile is ONE tap: it opens that tile's detail (an empty tile opens its explainer instead), and a tile's ⓘ explainer is on that detail view, not on the tile face.

sections.name: Apple Watch
tips: One-time setup: open the Strathlon app on the watch and tap Allow for Health. You only do this once per watch.

Start a session on the phone and Strathlon starts the workout on the watch automatically — live heart rate streams in and each block logs to Apple's Workout app with calories. No taps needed. A ⌚ shows when it's live.
Do NOT also start Apple's own Workout app for the same session — that double-counts calories.
Heart rate is colour-coded: amber = below target (push harder), red = at/above target.

Premium adds hands-free control: on the wrist, tap Done to log a set and start rest, tap again during rest to skip it - carries you from warm-up through the HIIT finisher. The ADVANCE controls (Done, Skip rest, Skip, Pause, Change, Continue) WAIT FOR YOUR PHONE: after a tap they show a spinner until the phone has received, run and acknowledged the command, so a tap that has not landed looks like one. NEXT UP's 'Start' is different: it sends nothing, opens a rest picker on the watch itself, and only the choice made there reaches the phone; the hand-off Start for the HIIT block does the same with a HIIT picker when the phone has sent a list to choose from. Both are disabled while another tap is pending. End, Finish and HIIT Stop stay tappable at all times, but the first tap asks 'End workout?'; the session ends on the confirm.
Apple's Fitness app lists workouts by duration, not calories; tap a workout to see calories — they ARE recorded.

The live warm-up and HIIT screens on the phone share one layout: a large progress ring with the countdown inside it, your stats down either side, a full-width primary control and a two-up row beneath it. Every control carries a visible word, not a bare symbol. The ending control on both screens is labelled End.

Warm-up and HIIT both have a Pause, on the phone and on the wrist. Pausing stops the Apple Watch workout session itself, not just the timer, so time spent paused is not added to your Apple Health exercise or energy.

The Apple Watch HIIT and warm-up screens now match the phone ones, and the app supports the watch always-on display: when you drop your wrist the session stays on the dimmed screen and the countdown keeps ticking rather than disappearing. If Low Power Mode is on the live screen names the real cost - buttons may not respond and heart rate is read less often - and both routes off: 'side button > battery % > Low Power Mode' now, and 'Settings > Workout' to stop it starting with every workout. Strathlon cannot switch it off; Apple does not permit that.

The calorie figure on the session completion screen always says where it came from: From your watch when a heart-rate-capable device recorded it, Estimated from heart rate when the app worked it out from your streamed pulse, or Estimated when there was no effort signal at all. When there is nothing to go on it shows a dash rather than a zero. It is never described as calories measured or burned -- Apple's active energy is itself a model output, and the app does not claim more certainty than it has.
No watch? Heart rate still comes from Apple Health where available.

sections.name: Activities, sports & goals
tips: Add a walk, run, cycle, swim, gym class, gym or home workout, or any sport to any day (including rest days) via 'Add activity'. IMPORTANT distinction: logging an activity here RAISES today's eating allowance so you can eat a bit more for it — that's the intake side. Recording the session in Apple Health (an Apple Watch workout, or a manual entry) separately raises the calories Apple Health shows you've BURNED — that's the other side of the same ledger. The two are meant to OFFSET each other, not add together: log the activity here for the eating allowance, and record it in Apple Health too so it also counts toward your burn. Add distance (km) to runs/walks for a sharper estimate; enter your own burn from a watch if you have it.
For gym classes, open Gym classes and search the name (e.g. 'rpm', 'bodypump'); calories scale to your weight and you can tweak duration or pin your own number.

For a gym or home workout, open the 'Gym & home' tile: pick Push/Pull/Leg/Upper day, a full-body/circuit, home bodyweight or home dumbbell — or 'Other workout (custom)'. Search by the name you use ('ppl', 'leg day', 'calisthenics'); calories scale to your weight and duration, or turn on Override to enter your own from a watch. It's for EXTRA or unplanned work — don't log your planned gym session here: it is already in your training-day target, and nothing stops it being counted twice.

Set each sport's Intensity (Light/Standard/High) to tune its calorie bonus: there is no Settings row called 'Sports' - it is Settings → 'NUTRITION & SPORT' → the 'N sports configured' card → 'Edit'. With multiple sports, reorder them in the 'SPORT PRIORITY' list on that same screen (shown only above one sport) - top is P1, and you can change it at any time, not just during setup. That order tunes your GYM work to your top two sports ONLY on the Sports Performance goal - without it there are no sport accessories at all and those slots refill from the ordinary goal pool. It does NOT set calorie bonuses. Calorie bonuses go by session SIZE: on a day with more than one session the largest earns the full bonus, a second counts at 55% and further ones at 30%, capped at 75% of BMR.

When a programme completes, switch to Maintenance: CALORIES rise to full TDEE over a 4-week reverse diet - rest-day maintenance less 200 and training-day less 250 in week 1, the gap shrinking each week (still 50 and 64 in week 4) and reaching full TDEE after week 4; carbs follow, being what is left after protein and fat. While Maintenance is on, the Nutrition tab opens on its Maintenance tab, whose headline is TODAY'S target - the same figure as the Tracker, whatever kind of day it is - with this week's training-day and rest-day figures beneath it; the Training, Rest, Match Day and Sport Training tabs each show that kind of day at this week's figures.

Going away? Plan tab → 'On a break or catching up?' saves the dates and asks WHAT KIND of break it is, because that sets what you eat. 'I'm on holiday' uses your MAINTENANCE calories, or your normal REST-DAY calories if those are higher — so it is never less than a normal rest day for you, with your plan paused. 'I can't train' (work, travel, illness) uses your REST-DAY calories, with your calorie plan carrying on — a deficit stays a deficit, a surplus stays a surplus, and calories near maintenance stay near maintenance. Neither pays for a session you are not doing; what you log while away still counts. While a holiday or can't-train break is on, the Nutrition tab opens on that allowance's own tab - Maintenance for a holiday, Rest for can't train - and its headline is TODAY'S target, the same figure as the Tracker, including anything you log; its other tabs still show what each kind of day is worth. No 'missed day' nagging; your plan pauses. Breaks saved before this update keep the targets they had - your training-day figure on a day with a gym session, your rest-day figure otherwise, with no scheduled sport session paid for - and the Nutrition tab opens on that Training or Rest tab, headlining the same figure as the Tracker. The same screen ticks days you trained while away.

sections.name: Privacy
tips: The 'Share my health data with the AI coach' switch (Settings -> App settings -> Privacy & your data) is the SINGLE permission for health data reaching the coach, covering: weight, BMI and body composition, metabolic rate (BMR), calories burned and the recent gap between what they ate and burned, heart rate, heart-rate variability (HRV) and between-set recovery, respiratory rate, blood oxygen (SpO2), overnight wrist temperature, cardio fitness (VO2 max), recent off-app workouts, a comparison of the activity they repeat most with their own earlier ones (never the route), the heart-rate shape of their most recent recorded session, today's steps, walking and running distance and exercise minutes, the split between resting and active calories burned, one-minute heart-rate recovery after training and walking heart rate compared with your own baseline, your sleep in detail (total sleep and sleep debt, the deep/REM/core/awake breakdown, how many times the night broke, sleep efficiency, and your bed and wake times), weight history, the derived readiness score, AND the user's hormone-therapy status if they have set one. It also covers the weigh-ins, burn and sleep behind the predicted-vs-actual card's 'Ask the coach about this' button. Off by default. On, the coach uses these WHEREVER asked - chat, Trends, reviews, the weight gap - with nothing more to confirm; off, they are not sent. NOT COVERED: the health & safety details the user typed in (always shared, next tip) and cycle (own switch).

The health & safety details the user TYPED IN THEMSELVES are always shared with the AI Coach on every message and are NOT controlled by the 'Share Health data' switch: allergies and supplements to avoid, pregnancy and breastfeeding, chronic conditions, medications, and injuries. This is deliberate - a coach that does not know about an allergy, a pregnancy or a heart medication could give unsafe advice. If a user asks what the coach knows about them, say this plainly; never tell them these details are withheld.

Food preferences are also always shared with the coach, including dietary or religious preferences such as halal, kosher, vegetarian or vegan, plus preferred cuisines and cooking time, so meal ideas suit the user.

Users can see the full list any time: Settings -> App settings -> Privacy & your data -> the ⓘ beside 'Share my health data with the AI coach' (the row of that name is gone; the ⓘ is the only way in).

What happens to the data sent to the AI: to keep follow-up questions fast, the AI provider briefly caches the BACKGROUND CONTEXT we send (a few minutes); beyond that our processors apply only their own limited operational retention, such as short-term abuse prevention. Strathlon keeps no long-term store of messages. On the phone itself one kind is kept: the chat clears each morning, but a message a coach-memory line was taken from is kept word for word and shown beside that line on 'What your coach remembers' until the line is removed. Do NOT tell a user their messages are simply 'discarded' - that overstates what we know. If someone asks whether their data is sold, used for advertising or used to train AI models, point them to the privacy policy and to the consent screen shown during onboarding rather than answering it from here.

Cycle-aware coaching is a separate, off-by-default switch; if on, the coach sees only a general phase label (e.g. 'pre-menstrual'). Strathlon never receives your dates, flow or symptoms, and neither does the AI. One thing does not depend on that switch: the optional 'Ease my targets in my pre-period week' option (also off by default) adds about 100 kcal to the Nutrition target around the period, and the coach sees that adjusted target plus a note that it was deliberately adjusted - never that the cycle is the reason, unless the phase-share switch is also on. Cycle features are also stood DOWN by default for a biological-female user who has told us they are on testosterone therapy, because periods commonly stop or become irregular on masculinising therapy; an 'I still menstruate' toggle in Settings -> Cycle-aware insights turns them straight back on.

Biological sex is ALWAYS shared with the AI Coach, alongside name and age, because the calorie model cannot be explained without it - it is shared as a number-driving fact and nothing more. HORMONE THERAPY is different: it is treated as sensitive health data, so it only reaches the coach when the 'Share my health data with the AI coach' switch is on. It is also left OUT of the iCloud backup unless the separate, off-by-default 'Back up health & safety details' switch is on. Setting it back to 'None' in Body & stats removes it everywhere.
Tell us an idea, share feedback or report a bug on the Feedback tab; browse and vote on what others have asked for on the Roadmap tab.

sections.name: Onboarding & your profile in detail
tips: You don't need an account, sign-up or password — your profile, logs and full history live on your device, so nothing to remember and nothing to lose to a forgotten password.

First-run setup builds the plan around you: your body details, your goal, your sport (pick from any category across 39 sports), and your weekly training/match schedule. You can edit these later in Settings. Changing your goal or experience keeps all your logged history and takes an automatic backup first; both routes to it are in the 'To edit anything later' tip below.

Manage your data in Settings → Reset & Data. RESTART: 'Restart my plan' puts your plan back to Week 1 today (keeps all history), and 'Restart and redo onboarding' lets you change your goal or experience (also keeps history). CLEAR SPECIFIC DATA: tick just what you want gone — Nutrition log, Weight & body, Lifting history, Holiday periods, Coach conversations, Coach's long-term memory or Cycle data — everything is off by default. What they clear goes from this device and their private iCloud backup. Coach conversations live on this device, so clearing removes their copy; what our AI provider holds is in the privacy policy. Two buckets keep something on purpose, and the app says so on screen: 'Weight & body' keeps measurements logged without a weight (a waist or chest entry on its own), and 'Lifting history' keeps the record of which exercises were ticked off each day. DELETE EVERYTHING: type DELETE to erase all your data and your iCloud backup and start fresh — that includes your saved foods, auto-add rules, saved meal plans, schedule changes, profile photo, any stored voice key, and (from build 211) your weight-stack photos, any data export you made, your saved shopping lists and the record of which exercises you ticked off on which day. Nothing is copied back from Strathlon afterwards. Apple Health is the exception, and only because that data is not ours: weigh-ins Health holds are untouched — Strathlon only ever reads them, never writes them — so your weight chart fills back in from Health. Weigh-ins you typed into Strathlon are deleted for good, and if anything cannot be removed the app tells the user rather than reporting a clean wipe. ONE EXCEPTION, stated on both delete screens: workouts Strathlon saved to Apple Health stay in Apple's Health app — they are the user's and they live in Apple's app, so delete them from Health if they want them gone. Clearing Cycle data asks a second time and never touches Apple Health. It cannot be undone and Strathlon keeps no hidden recoverable copy, so use 'Export my data first' (a CSV + JSON copy) at the top of that screen before you clear or delete.

The readiness check is a short, optional set of yes/no questions — the kind a trainer asks before you start. If an answer stands out, Strathlon gently suggests getting medical clearance first. It is a readiness check, not medical advice. Strathlon never receives your individual answers and neither does your coach: it is told only that a readiness item was flagged (and whether clearance was confirmed), so it can keep guidance conservative.

You are asked ONCE, in onboarding, whether the AI Coach may see your Apple Health figures; it is off by default and changeable any time with the 'Share my health data with the AI coach' switch in Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data.

To edit anything later: Settings. 'Body & stats' holds your measurements, your units and the 'Week starts on' preference. YOUR GOAL WEIGHT IS EDITABLE ON ITS OWN (build 213) - Settings → 'Goal & plan' → the 'GOAL WEIGHT' section - so NEVER tell a user to redo onboarding just to change their target weight. Your GOAL ITSELF (fat loss / muscle gain / general fitness / sports performance) and your EXPERIENCE LEVEL are different and remain read-only wherever they are shown, because they reshape the whole plan - change those via 'Goal & plan' → 'Change goal or experience' → 'Redo onboarding', or via Reset & Data → 'Restart and redo onboarding' (the same flow either way, and history is kept). The Health-data sharing switch is under App settings → Privacy & your data, and cycle-phase sharing under HEALTH → Cycle-aware insights.

Resting heart rate and VO2 max are optional in setup and must be realistic to be accepted: resting HR between 30 and 150 bpm, VO2 max between 10 and 100 ml/kg/min. If you enter something outside that it is not saved -- and if you already had a value saved, that one is kept -- and the field tells you which happened. You can change both later without redoing setup: Settings -> Body & stats has a Resting HR and a VO2 max stepper. Settings -> Your targets shows your age-based maximum HR as a single figure. There is no heart-rate-zone breakdown. Your resting heart rate is now taken from Apple Health when a real reading exists, otherwise from what you entered here; if there is neither, the app uses a typical adult figure and says so rather than presenting it as yours. The only thing that reads it is the AI coach's context.

BMR AND HORMONE THERAPY. Strathlon works out BMR in one of TWO ways, and Settings -> Your targets -> 'BMR formula' always names which one is running. (1) If a measured body-fat % or lean mass is available (body composition switched ON), BMR comes from that MEASURED value via Katch-McArdle - the most accurate route, and it always wins regardless of any hormone-therapy answer; a user who has body composition switched OFF stays on branch (2) no matter what they answer on hormone therapy. (2) Otherwise BMR is the standard weight-based Mifflin-St Jeor estimate from weight, height, age and biological sex - the equation itself is NEVER swapped - and if the user is on hormone therapy a bounded kcal adjustment is added on top: body-fat is estimated from height, weight and age for the user's biological sex, shifted HALF of the way toward the body composition that therapy tends to produce, clamped to a physiological range, and the resulting change in implied lean mass is converted into a kcal delta. COUNTER-INTUITIVE CASE: for a user whose therapy pushes in the SAME direction their birth sex already sits (a male-born user on testosterone, a female-born user on estrogen), that shift is clamped out entirely and the delta is EXACTLY ZERO - their calories are byte-identical to what they'd be without answering the hormone question, so never tell a user in this case that their estimate was 'shifted'. The 'BMR formula' row reads one of three values: 'Katch-McArdle' (measured), 'Weight-based (hormone-adjusted)' (branch 2 with a non-zero delta applied), or 'Weight-based' (branch 2, no delta, including everyone not on hormone therapy). 'Katch-McArdle (estimated)' no longer exists as a value - never use it. Adding a real body-fat % in Body & stats always replaces any weight-based estimate. The minimum daily calorie floor is keyed to biological sex and the hormone adjustment can never push a user below it. Tap the info icon next to Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) in Your targets for the same explanation in plain English.

GOAL WEIGHT EDITOR (build 213). Settings → 'Goal & plan' → 'GOAL WEIGHT'. It is the SAME stepper, the same three warning banners and the same rules as the last screen of onboarding - one shared component, not a second copy - so advice given about one is true of the other. Underneath the stepper it states what the target means: how far there is to go, how many training weeks remain in the plan, and the weekly rate that implies. IF THE PACE IS FASTER THAN A STEADY ONE IT SAYS SO AND STILL LETS THE USER SAVE - a target is a goal, not a schedule, so do not treat that message as a block. The ONLY thing that disables 'Save goal weight' is a target that CONTRADICTS the goal (a fat-loss target above current weight, or a gain target below it); the button also stays disabled when nothing has actually been changed, and reads 'Saved' once a target is stored and untouched. Changing the goal weight re-derives goal progress, the end-of-plan branch and the 'X to go' line, and it does NOT rebuild the plan and does NOT re-anchor where the journey started - the distance already covered is kept. It DOES move calories (build 228): the fat-loss deficit is the gap to the goal weight spread over the weeks LEFT in the plan, held down by the safe-pace cap, the calorie floor and the PAR-Q cap - so a new target changes the daily calorie targets and the carb figure derived from them. Protein and fat come from the body, not the goal, and do not move.

WEEK STARTS ON (build 213). Settings → 'Body & stats' → 'Week starts on' - a Sun / Mon choice, DEFAULT SUNDAY. It changes which day the Plan tab's THIS WEEK strip and the sport calendar begin on, and both move together. IT IS A DISPLAY SETTING ONLY, and this is the part to get right when asked: WEEKLY REVIEWS AND TRAINING STREAKS ALWAYS RUN MONDAY TO SUNDAY whichever way this is set, so flipping it never relabels a week already trained and never changes a past review. The weekly schedule the user set in onboarding is unaffected - a Wednesday gym day is still Wednesday; only which seven dates the strip spans changes. The AI coach reads the week the same way round as the Plan tab does, so 'this week' means the same seven days in the chat as on screen.

sections.name: Running a workout, timers & supersets
tips: The workout screen is split into fold-out sections — warm-up, your main workout, and - from Phase 2 onwards, so a Phase 1 day has none - a HIIT finisher. Warm-up and HIIT start folded to cut scrolling; your main workout stays open. Tap any header to collapse or expand it.

Warm-up, rest and HIIT countdowns keep running on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island with spoken cues, so you can put the phone down between sets. The voice coach calls each exercise and set including the rep target, with a 3-2-1 into each work set.

Some training days end with a HIIT finisher and a short core finisher (such as plank, dead bug or glute bridge march). It tops up to 2 core moves for the day in total, counting any core work your sport accessories already include — so it may add 0, 1 or 2 moves — and it never repeats the same movement pattern (e.g. rotational) twice. Core is added on every strength day, MAINTENANCE days included from build 230 (built from the maintenance core spec, so longer holds) — never on rest or sport-only days — and it rotates week to week. A gym-plus-sport double day IS a strength day, so it does get core work.

Both the HIIT finisher and the core finisher adapt to any injury you flag. HIIT filters its movements for all injury types (a shoulder injury hides overhead and forceful-arm moves; a lower-back injury hides jumps, hinges and crunches; an elbow injury hides gripping moves; knee/ankle keep the low-impact set), always leaving a full set of safe options. Nothing is shown on the card: the 'Adapted for: <your injuries>' heading lives behind the HIIT card's ⓘ, by an owner decision in build 218. The core finisher likewise only ever shows core work that is safe for your injuries.
Log working weight × reps on any exercise (pre-filled from last time), or choose 'Log each set' for per-set detail. Enter kg or lb. Bodyweight moves can be saved with a weight of 0.

Subscribers can tap 'Snap to fill' to photograph a dumbbell, plate or machine display and Strathlon reads the number off it. A LOADED BARBELL is handled differently, because no single figure in that photo is the weight you lifted: a confirm sheet asks three things - your bar's weight (20 kg unless you change it, and it remembers), what is on ONE SIDE of the bar (filled in from the photo), and, if the maths is still wrong, the total typed by you, which always wins. It shows its working, and it still opens when the plates cannot be read. Nothing goes into the weight field until you tap the total, and nothing is saved until you tap Save. Weights then auto-fill next time, so you just confirm or nudge them.

Where the plan pairs exercises into groups, each group header has its own switch. Leave it on to run that group back-to-back as a superset/tri-set; turn it off to do those exercises one at a time as straight sets, each with its own start button and rest between every set. The app remembers the choice per pairing, so a combination that never works at your gym stays as straight sets; a pairing that has not appeared in your plan for six weeks is forgotten and runs as a superset again. On a switched-off group, tap the info button on its header for how to keep the same training density.

Trained away from the app or your phone? Tap 'Mark this session done' so it counts toward PHASE PROGRESSION - and only that, as the button says: not your streaks, your charts or the block's session count (works for earlier days too); tap again to undo. Sessions captured automatically (a guided session or an Apple Watch workout) stay locked so real training is never removed by accident.

HOW A DAY IS BALANCED, AND THE PHASE-1 CEILING (build 213). In PHASE 1 only, on its straight-set days, three rules are applied to the assembled day - the gym lifts and the sport accessories together, not the core finisher (phases 2 and 3 serve their authored supersets and tri-sets untouched, so a Phase-2 pressing day carries no guarantee of a row or a pulldown): (1) no two exercises in the day train the same movement pattern; (2) a day that presses must also carry a ROW and a PULLDOWN OR CHIN; (3) pulling sets must reach at least 80% of pressing sets. Where the user's equipment or the day genuinely cannot supply a missing movement, the rule STANDS DOWN and leaves the exercise that was already there - a session is never made SHORTER to satisfy a rule. A dedicated Push day balances against its paired Pull day rather than within itself, which is what a push/pull split is for. The rules keep the first row of each movement pattern and give up rows from the END of the day, so the day's FIRST exercise normally stays in place - with one exception: if it is the day's only upper-body isolation move (a dumbbell curl, say) and the day still needs more pulling, that first exercise is the row traded for a pull. YOU can still swap any row, the first included, with 'Swap this exercise'. And when a sport accessory collides with a gym movement it is the SPORT move that is swapped, not the main lift. SEPARATELY, PHASE 1 (Reactivation) IS CAPPED AT 8 EXERCISES for the whole assembled day - roughly 24 working sets - because it is the easing-back-in block; sport accessories and the core finisher are NEVER what gets cut, only the main lifts are trimmed, and the trim keeps the press, the row, the pulldown and the leg work in preference to isolation, even when the isolation move is the day's first exercise. A phase-1 user with NO sport is normally under the ceiling already and sees no change. PHASES 2 AND 3 HAVE NO WHOLE-DAY CEILING, though in every phase a day that adds sport accessories (or, off the Sports Performance goal, the rows that replace them) holds its main lifts plus those rows to 8. None of this changes calorie burn: burn is worked out separately from the displayed session duration.

'Swap this exercise' on an expanded exercise card replaces that row in one tap with another from the same category, free, on any row that is not finished or in progress - the day's first exercise included; where there is nothing to offer, the card says 'No swap available' and why. The choice is REMEMBERED for the rest of the plan: the row then says it is standing in for the original and offers an Undo, and a 'Remembered swaps' row appears in Settings once you have one.

To change how long you rest: a 'Rest 60s — change' chip (showing the rest actually set) sits under the Start button. It opens the rest picker - 45, 60 or 90 seconds, or 2 minutes; 60 by default - and the choice is REMEMBERED and used for every exercise from then on without asking again. On a superset or tri-set group the same chip sits under the group's Start and sets the rest between rounds.

On a training day the sport-specific accessory work sits at the END of the main block, under its own header named for your sport ('CRICKET — SPORT WORK') with an ⓘ saying why it is there. Where a sport move is itself a core movement it takes one of the day's two core slots and the core finisher below is shortened rather than repeating it. You only get this block on the Sports Performance goal.

sections.name: History, export & data ownership
tips: 'All days', at the foot of the Tracker's CALENDAR tile, opens your whole history newest first, with calories in, calories out and weight for each day. Tap a day to open it and 'Edit this day's log' to change it.

Missed a day, or got one wrong? Tracker → the ＋ button in the top bar opens 'Add or fix a day'. Pick any date from today back through the last two years — further if your own history goes back further — then 'Open this day'. The day opens on its own screen: 'Edit this day's log' for calories consumed and burned (burned is pulled from Apple Health where it has data) and your weight, and 'Add activity' to add a walk, run or session to THAT day rather than to today. Today's burn is live from Apple Health (whichever device or app writes it there — an Apple Watch if you wear one, otherwise your iPhone's motion sensors). When Apple Health has no burn data for today at all, the Burned and Deficit/Surplus/Balance tiles show a dash rather than a zero, so no deficit or surplus is implied.

Picking a date you have ALREADY logged is safe: the picker says so before you open it, and the day shows what it holds before you change anything. Saving from 'Edit this day's log' updates only the boxes shown — your logged food items and your protein/carbs/fat are always kept. Leaving a box empty means 'leave that value as it is', not zero.
To correct just a weigh-in for a past day, open that day from the ＋ button, tap 'Edit this day's log' and change only the weight — the calorie boxes can be left empty.
Use the ⋯ button in the Tracker's top bar → 'Import / Export logs' for a CSV round-trip of your daily log, so your data is portable and yours to keep.

Every backup below goes to their OWN private iCloud, never to a Strathlon server - what DOES reach us is the next tip, and FOUR smaller channels, also described in Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data: PUSH REGISTRATION, gated by 'Product updates' and DEFAULT ON, which uploads an APNs device token - the app's only device identifier - with platform, environment, build and topics, at most once a day; failure reports, which say which step failed and carry nothing about the user off the phone (our server adds the country), and which they can switch off; anything they choose to send through Feedback & Requests, including an email address if they give one; and a barcode their phone looks up directly with a public food database, which sees their internet address. Never claim the coach payload is the only thing that reaches us. In Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data you control each backup separately: 'iCloud backup' (on by default) covers your basic details, weight, daily totals, goals, training setup, plan progress and food preferences; the day totals it mirrors leave out the individual food items, so a restore brings back their numbers rather than what they ate; 'Back up training data to iCloud' (ON by default) covers your weigh-ins and your logged sets, each capped to the trailing five years, plus your declared holiday breaks, which are synced in full for as long as you keep them; 'Back up health & safety details' and 'Sync progress photos to iCloud' are each OFF by default and cover your allergies/injuries/conditions and your progress photos respectively. Cycle dates, flow, symptoms and history are in none; one cycle-derived detail rides 'Back up health & safety details' - whether they still menstruate.

Meals and photos DO go to a Cloudflare Worker Strathlon runs, which passes them to the AI provider: today's and yesterday's food by name with calories and macros, the foods they repeat at each meal over a rolling 21 days, one especially regular food with the days they logged it and its average calories, plus any attached photo. Each request is logged with its size, cost, feature and model, a short code naming the rule that chose that model (for example a named food, a photo or a Progress tile question), plus the subscription identifier Apple gives us - not the message content. Never say these are not uploaded to us. Strathlon reads the figures the user permits and writes nothing back from the phone; if they use Strathlon on an Apple Watch, the watch app saves the workouts it records to Apple Health - that is the only thing Strathlon writes.
Change units (kg / lb / stone) any time in Settings → Body & Stats → Units; the whole app reflows and your saved data is unchanged underneath.

If you reinstall or move to a new phone and restore your backup, your health & safety details will NOT come back unless you had turned 'Back up health & safety details' on — it is off by default. Strathlon warns you before you restore and keeps a reminder at the top of your Settings tab until you re-enter them, because until you do, your meals and plan cannot take your allergies, injuries, conditions or medications into account.

sections.name: Notifications, nuggets & learning
tips: A daily knowledge nugget card surfaces a short, evidence-based tip; some nuggets carry a 'Learn more' link that opens a fuller article on strathlon.com.

Three local notifications are ON by default, controlled in Settings → App settings → Notifications & Tips: 'Daily tip notification' (one science-backed tip each morning, around 9am), 'Bedtime reminder' (a gentle nightly wind-down reminder, with extra recovery emphasis after a hard training day; its time is set from your own recent sleep and is adjustable in that screen between 8pm and 11:30pm, falling back to 10:45pm without enough sleep data) and 'Progress updates'. Notification permission is asked once, near the end of onboarding — if declined, they stay switched on in Settings but won't actually notify until permission is granted (Settings app → Notifications → Strathlon), and Strathlon never re-prompts automatically. A FOURTH switch is default ON and is not on that screen: 'Product updates', under Settings → App settings → Privacy & your data, is a server-side push channel: while it is on and notifications are allowed, the phone registers a push token with Strathlon's server, at most once a day.

'Progress updates' tells you when there is something to read: your weekly review, today's readiness, a report for a workout you recorded outside Strathlon, a streak week about to close, a new working weight, a tile coming alive, a health tile whose verdict turns to its improving case (at most once per tile every 30 days, with the verdict itself as the message), or the recap of a session you finished in Strathlon — that one with a one-tap effort rating. Tapping one opens the exact tile, review or report it is about, not just the app. Ten a day is the WHOLE app's notification budget - these, the daily tip, the bedtime reminder, the coach-memory review notice and the server push all spend it - and never two in the same morning or the same evening; the recap answers something you just did, so it is not rationed — one per training day, none between 10pm and 7am. Ignore five in a row and the channel narrows to the weekly review alone; five more and it goes quiet until you next open Progress. On a morning one arrives, the daily tip waits for the next free day. A body only carries figures that cannot move: the readiness score, a finished workout's distance, time and calories, and a finished session's exercises, sets, minutes and rest.

Deeper guides and evidence articles live on the website — the Learn library, per-stat explainer pages, and topic guides (building muscle, fat loss, training with your cycle, supplements, recovery, habits). Ask the Coach and it can point you to the relevant one.
